tagline: Up the rail grade beside a creek that freezes upside down.
intro: From Spearfish, at the mouth of the canyon, US 14A climbs south for 19 miles with Spearfish Creek as its guide, under limestone walls where spruce, pine, aspen, birch and oak hold to the slopes. The road lies on an old railroad grade, abandoned after massive flooding in 1933, and Savoy and Elmore were stops on the line.
The creek runs fast enough that in winter it freezes from the bottom up. Frank Lloyd Wright visited the canyon in 1935 and later wondered why the East had heard so much more about the Grand Canyon.
season: September, when the aspens turn and the canyon becomes a favorite fall color drive.

moments.title: Bridal Veil Falls
moments.text: About six miles in, the falls come down a sheer 60-foot cliff right beside the road, on a stretch where mountain goats brought to the Black Hills in the 1920s are often seen.

moments.title: Roughlock Falls
moments.text: From Savoy a walking trail leads to the spot where Little Spearfish Creek becomes a waterfall, and the final winter scene of Dances with Wolves was filmed farther along the gravel road.

moments.title: Cheyenne Crossing
moments.text: The last of eleven stops on the Cheyenne to Deadwood stage route, where tired horses were traded for fresh ones before the final showy run into Deadwood.

practical: Dispersed camping is not allowed in Spearfish Canyon.
